風邪、病院、薬局、なくし物。いざというときに落ち着いて症状や状況を伝えられる、安: Colds, hospitals, pharmacies, lost items. Chinese for peace of mind, so you can calmly explain your symptoms or situation when something goes wrong.
薬局で症状を伝える: Describing your symptoms at a pharmacy
深圳に出張して三日目の吉田さん。冷房の効いたオフィスと蒸し暑い外を行き来するうち: It's Yuto Yoshida's third day on a business trip to Shenzhen. Going back and forth between the air-conditioned office and the muggy outdoors, he has had a sore throat and felt feverish since last night. He has another important meeting tomorrow. Before work, he hurries into a pharmacy with a green cross sign near his hotel. A clerk in a white coat calls out to him from the counter.
薬局の店員、三十代。薬剤師の資格を持ち、説明が丁寧で落ち着いている: Pharmacy clerk in her thirties. A licensed pharmacist who explains things carefully and calmly.
大阪の会社から深圳に出張中の日本人、三十歳。中国語は簡単な日常会話ができる: Japanese employee of an Osaka company on a business trip in Shenzhen, 30. He can handle simple everyday conversation in Chinese.
薬局の店員とお客さん。店員さんは専門知識を持つ相談相手で、症状を具体的に聞いてき: A pharmacy clerk and a customer. The clerk is an expert you can consult, and she will ask about your symptoms in detail. For the customer, describing symptoms accurately matters more than being polite. If you hold back and downplay your symptoms, you may be recommended medicine that doesn't suit you.
こんにちは、どうされましたか。: Hello, what seems to be the problem?
「哪里不舒服？」は直訳すると「どこが具合悪いですか」。薬局や病院で最初に必ず聞か: 「哪里不舒服？」 literally means "Where do you feel unwell?" It's always the first question at a pharmacy or hospital. 「不舒服」 is a handy word for feeling unwell in general.
少し熱があって、喉もすごく痛いんです。: I have a bit of a fever, and my throat really hurts.
「嗓子」は喉、「疼」は痛い。「痛」も使えますが、話し言葉では「疼」が一般的です。: 「嗓子」 means "throat," and 「疼」 means "to hurt." 「痛」 can also be used, but 「疼」 is more common in speech. 「有点儿」 means "a little," but if your symptoms are severe, use 「很」 or 「特别」 and be honest about how bad it is.
熱は何度ですか。体温は測りましたか。: How high is your fever? Have you taken your temperature?
昨日の夜は三十八度でした。今日は少しよくなりました。: It was 38 degrees last night. It's a little better today.
咳は出ますか。鼻水は？: Do you have a cough? A runny nose?
咳は少しあります。鼻水は出ません。: I'm coughing a little, but no runny nose.
風邪かもしれませんね。何かお薬のアレルギーはありますか。: It's probably a cold. Are you allergic to any medications?
「过敏」はアレルギー。「我对青霉素过敏」（ペニシリンにアレルギーがあります）のよ: 「过敏」 means "allergy." You say it with 「对...过敏」, as in 「我对青霉素过敏」 ("I'm allergic to penicillin"). If you have a chronic condition or allergies, keep a note in Chinese on your phone so that in an emergency you only need to show it.
ありません。その薬、飲むと眠くなりますか。明日も仕事があるので。: No. Will this medicine make me drowsy? I have to work tomorrow.
「犯困」は眠くなること。仕事や運転の予定があるときは、自分から確認しておくと安心: 「犯困」 means "to get drowsy." If you have work or driving planned, asking about it yourself gives you peace of mind. At Chinese pharmacies, besides Western medicine (「西药」), you may also be recommended 「中成药」, ready-made traditional Chinese medicines.
これは大丈夫です。一日三回、一回二錠、食後に飲んでください。: This one won't. Three times a day, two tablets each time, after meals.
一日三回、一回二錠、食後ですね。メモしておきます。: Three times a day, two tablets each time, after meals. Let me write that down.
薬の飲み方は、聞いたままを繰り返して確認するのが一番安全です。「片」は錠剤を数え: The safest way to check how to take medicine is to repeat back exactly what you heard. 「片」 is the measure word for tablets. The number "two" becomes 「两」 before a measure word, so you say 「两片」.
もし三日たってもよくならなかったら、必ず病院に行ってくださいね。: If you're not better in three days, be sure to go see a doctor.
わかりました。マスクも一箱ください。全部でいくらですか。: Okay. I'll also get a box of masks. How much is it altogether?
全部で五十五元です。お湯をたくさん飲んで、ゆっくり休んでくださいね！: 55 altogether. Drink plenty of hot water and get some good rest!
「多喝热水」は中国でいちばんよく聞く気遣いの言葉。体を温めて休むのが大事、という: 「多喝热水」 is the most commonly heard expression of concern in China. It comes from the idea that warming your body and resting are what matter. It's such a staple that it has become a running joke online, but when someone says it to you, just accept it graciously with 「谢谢」.
「我有点儿不舒服」＝ちょっと具合が悪いです。体調全般に使える: 「我有点儿不舒服」 = I'm feeling a bit unwell. Can be used for any kind of physical discomfort.
「发高烧」＝高熱が出る。熱の温度は「三十八度」のように言う: 「发高烧」 = to have a high fever. Temperatures are given like 「三十八度」 (38 degrees).
「嗓子疼」＝喉が痛い。「嗓子哑了」＝声がかれた: 「嗓子疼」 = sore throat; 「嗓子哑了」 = to have lost one's voice
「头疼」「肚子疼」「牙疼」。部位 + 疼 で何でも言える: 「头疼」, 「肚子疼」, 「牙疼」. Body part + 「疼」 lets you describe any pain.
「量」は測る。「量血压」＝血圧を測る: 「量」 means "to measure." 「量血压」 = to take someone's blood pressure
「咳嗽得厉害」＝咳がひどい: 「咳嗽得厉害」 = to have a bad cough
「鼻子堵了」＝鼻が詰まった: 「鼻子堵了」 = to have a stuffy nose
日本語と同じ漢字。「我感冒了」＝風邪をひきました: 「我感冒了」 = I've caught a cold.
「对〜过敏」の形で使う。花粉症は「花粉过敏」: Used in the form 「对...过敏」. Hay fever is 「花粉过敏」
「吃了会犯困吗？」＝飲むと眠くなりますか: 「吃了会犯困吗？」 = Will it make me drowsy?
錠剤を数える量詞。「一次两片」＝一回二錠: The measure word for tablets. 「一次两片」 = two tablets each time
「饭前」＝食前。薬の袋にもよく書いてある: 「饭前」 = before meals. Often written on medicine packets too.
「一盒口罩」＝マスク一箱: 「一盒口罩」 = a box of masks
緑の十字の看板が目印。大きな店には薬剤師がいる: Look for the green cross sign. Larger stores have pharmacists.
症状を伝える最も基本的な形。部位の言葉さえわかれば、何でも言えます。痛みの強さは: The most basic pattern for describing symptoms. As long as you know the word for the body part, you can say anything. Adjust the intensity with 「有点儿」 (a little), 「很」 (very), and 「特别」 (really). Many people tend to tough it out and downplay pain, but in medical situations, accurately describing how bad it is protects you.
少し頭が痛いです。: I have a bit of a headache.
お腹がすごく痛くて、昨日の夜からなんです。: My stomach really hurts. It started last night.
アレルギーを伝える大切な表現。病院、薬局、レストランで、命に関わることもあるので: An important expression for telling people about allergies. At hospitals, pharmacies, and restaurants it can be a matter of life and death, so if it applies to you, be sure to learn it. 「对」 means "toward." If you have none, answer 「我没有过敏」.
ピーナッツアレルギーなので、料理に入れないでください。: I'm allergic to peanuts, so please don't put any peanuts in the dish.
「如果」と同じく仮定を表しますが、より話し言葉的。医師や薬剤師の注意事項でよく使: Like 「如果」, it expresses a hypothetical, but it's more colloquial. It's often used in doctors' and pharmacists' instructions to tell you what to do next, as in 「要是还不好，就去医院」 ("If you're not better, go to the hospital"). Make sure you don't miss it.
もし三日たってもよくならなければ、必ず病院へ。: If you're not better in three days, be sure to go to the hospital.
高熱が出たら、電話してね。: If you get a high fever, give me a call.
具合が悪いなら、早めに帰りなよ。: If you're not feeling well, go home early.
薬局、病院の受付や診察、会社で体調不良を伝えるときなど。「どこが」「いつから」「: At a pharmacy, at hospital reception or in an exam, when telling your company you're unwell, and so on. If you say "where," "since when," and "how bad" in that order, the other person will understand the situation right away. Always repeat back how to take your medicine to confirm it.
「大丈夫です」が口癖の日本人は、症状を軽く言いがち。「有点儿」ばかり使うと、本当: If "I'm fine" is your reflex, you'll tend to downplay your symptoms. If you only ever say 「有点儿」, you'll be given only mild medicine even when you're really suffering. Also, nodding along with 「好的」 to explanations you don't understand is especially dangerous when it comes to medicine.
薬局の店員さんは、外国人のお客さんが症状をうまく言えなくても、一生懸命聞き出そう: Pharmacy clerks will try hard to draw out information even if a foreign customer can't describe their symptoms well. When you describe things specifically, they'll want to make sure you get better and will carefully explain everything, down to drug interactions and lifestyle precautions.
慣れない土地で体調を崩すと、言葉の不安も重なって心細くなります。でも中国の薬局は: Getting sick in an unfamiliar place, with language worries on top of it, can make you feel very alone. But pharmacies in China are everywhere in town, and they're a reliable place where you can easily ask for advice. The important thing is not to tough it out. Many people downplay their symptoms or put work first because they don't want to be a bother, but if things get worse, you'll cause even more worry. Speaking up honestly and early isn't weakness; it's the responsible thing to do. Tell a coworker 「我感冒了」 and they'll probably bring you hot water with a 「多喝热水！」. Accept that warmth and get well soon.
薬局で「哪里不舒服？」と聞かれました。どういう意味？: At a pharmacy you're asked 「哪里不舒服？」. What does it mean?
「不舒服」は具合が悪いこと。薬局や病院で最初に聞かれる質問です。: 「不舒服」 means feeling unwell. It's the first question you'll be asked at a pharmacy or hospital.
「喉がとても痛い」と伝える自然な言い方は？: What is a natural way to say "My throat really hurts"?
「部位 + 很疼」が基本形。喉は「嗓子」と言います。: Body part + 「很疼」 is the basic pattern. The throat is called 「嗓子」.
「次」は回数、「片」は錠剤の量詞。「一天三次，一次两片」で一日三回、一回二錠です: 「次」 counts times, and 「片」 is the measure word for tablets. 「一天三次，一次两片」 means three times a day, two tablets each time.
ピーナッツアレルギーを伝えたいとき、正しいのは？: Which is correct for saying you have a peanut allergy?
「对〜过敏」の語順で言います。アレルギーは命に関わることもあるので正確に。: Use the word order 「对...过敏」. Allergies can be life-threatening, so say it accurately.
